Service Requirements The Contractor must provide printing services, including the following tasks: • Graphic design and creation of annual report content for various Embassy offices. • Graphic design and creation of brochures, information portfolios, folders, advertising publications, flyers, and similar materials for the Embassy's promotional events. • Printing and/or photocopying of documents, brochures, and portfolios in a professional manner, ensuring clear colors, photographs, text, and images for finished products. Preference will be given to contractors offering multiple printing methods, such as commercial, digital, press, and web-based printing. • Supplying stock images for publications, as needed. • Providing printing designs for requesting offices to review and confirm prior to production. The Contractor is responsible for installing, setting up, and delivering printed items to U.S. Embassy Hanoi events. • Material Requirements: The Contractor shall present several material options for the Embassy's selection prior to submitting a quote. Services must include all necessary supplies — such as equipment, toner, developer, fuser agent, staples, paper, g

Grant No.: TF0D0285 

Assignment Title: Consultancy Service for Operational Readiness, Systems Integration, Commissioning, Go-Live Management and Operational Stabilization of East Container Terminal (ECT)

deliverables_scope.text: cession pipeline locations currently relies on labor- intensive, manual measurements and standard-size charts. No automated capability currently exists to capture updates to changes in this data over the Soldiers’ career. This highly variable process heavily depends on the consistency of the personnel taking the measurements and cannot effectively scale to support remote or pre-arrival processing or updates to the Soldiers’ data over time. Because accurate sizing data is typically unavailable until a Soldier or Cadet is physically present, the Army cannot accurately predict and translate individual measurements into precise outfitting requirements prior to the point of initial issue. For geographically dispersed populations, such as West Point and Senior ROTC Cadets who matriculate across hundreds of universities without visiting a MEPS facility, 3 there is no standardized mechanism to collect pre-arrival sizing data. As soldiers progress through their careers, measurements change, which results in incorrect measurement data used for training equipment, new solder equipment fielding, and deployment preparations. Consequently, this data gap creates significant logistical bottlenecks: a lengthy initial- issue process, a high rate of poorly fitting uniforms and boot

tact methods and translating those measurements into recommended standard Army uniform and footwear sizes. Accurate measurement-to-size mapping — not a 3D visual try-on or avatar rendering, is the core capability sought. The Army is seeking a solution that will operate reliably across a wide spectrum of Army operating environments, minimize the training burden on Soldiers and administering staff, and be capable of integrating with designated Army data systems to support downstream sizing and issue processes. 3. REQUIRED AND DESIRED SOLUTION ATTRIBUTES. Required Attributes: The proposed solution shall meet the following mandatory requirements: • Comprehensive Scanning and Environmental Resilience: Must capture both body and foot measurements sufficient to determine standard Army uniform and footwear sizing using automated, digital, non-contact methods that eliminate manual measurements. The capture hardware must be transportable and capable of operating reliably across a wide spectrum of environments, including indoor facilities and austere outdoor settings, accommodating real-world conditions such as variable ambient lighting and physical space constraints. • Data Translation & Mapping: Must translate captured body and foot measurements into recommended standard Army

ughput: Batch processing at MEPS and IET Reception facilities. o Remote Self-Assessment: A mobile self-service assessment accessible via standard smart devices for geographically dispersed individuals. This includes pre-accession Cadets and in-service Soldiers requiring sizing for pre-deployment, unit-level equipment fielding, or periodic data updates in both garrison and austere field environments. • Usability: Must be highly intuitive, requiring minimal training for both the Soldiers and Cadets being measured and the administering staff. • Security & Compliance: Must comply with all applicable DoD Risk Management Framework (RMF) requirements and be capable of obtaining the appropriate Authorization to Operate (ATO) prior to processing any Soldier and Cadet data (all captured data must be encrypted at rest and in transit). Impact Level 5 (IL5) is required prior to full-scale enterprise deployment. Pilot execution will be conducted in an isolated, test/dummy network environment. • Data Management & Privacy: Must support a defined data retention and deletion schedule that strictly adheres to Army records-management and Privacy Act requirements. • Inclusive Accuracy: Must produce accurate measurements across the complete spectrum of body types, statures, and physical com

asured and the administering staff. • Security & Compliance: Must comply with all applicable DoD Risk Management Framework (RMF) requirements and be capable of obtaining the appropriate Authorization to Operate (ATO) prior to processing any Soldier and Cadet data (all captured data must be encrypted at rest and in transit). The Army is exploring a Sizing Technology Pilot to modernize the Soldier and Cadet outfitting process by using body scanning, foot scanning, computer vision, and/or AI- driven measurement extraction to generate accurate measurements and translate them into recommended uniform and footwear sizing. The scope of this requirement encompasses both body and foot scanning to modernize the issuance of both uniforms and footwear. No automated capability currently exists to capture updates to changes in this data over the Soldiers’ career. s. Uniform and footwear sizing for Army Soldiers at accession pipeline locations currently relies on labor- intensive, manual measurements and standard-size charts. No automated capability currently exists to capture updates to changes in this data over the Soldiers’ career. This highly variable process heavily depends on the consistency of the personnel taking the measurements and cannot effectively scale to support remote or pre-arrival processing or updates to the Soldiers’ data over time. Because accurate sizing data is typically unavailable until a Soldier or Cadet is physically present, the Army cannot accurately predict and translate individual measurements into precise outfitting requirements prior to the point of initial issue. For geographically dispersed populations, such as West Point and Senior ROTC Cadets who matriculate across hundreds of universities without visiting a MEPS facility, 3 there is no standardized mechanism to collect pre-arrival sizing data. As soldiers progress through their careers, measurements change, which results in incorrect measurement data used for training equipment, new solder equipment fielding, and deployment preparations. ielding, and deployment preparations. Consequently, this data gap creates significant logistical bottlenecks: a lengthy initial- issue process, a high rate of poorly fitting uniforms and boots, downstream exchanges, and an inconsistent experience across different geographic locations. At the tactical and operational levels, these sizing inaccuracies lead to excess inventory of mis-forecasted sizes and highly inefficient supply chain management. To address these challenges, the Army is seeking a commercial solution capable of accurately capturing both body and foot measurements using automated, digital, non- contact methods and translating those measurements into recommended standard Army uniform and footwear sizes. Procurements exceeding $5,000 up to $100,000 are normally provided by small businesses utilizing the AOC small business set-aside program i

The design team must review compliance with the building program at each stage of the project to ensure the requirements of the program, AOC Facility Standards and relevant codes and standards have been met. General Building Standards: Quality of Architectural/Engineering Design: The designs of new facilities should not detract from those that exist presently, and designs for rehabilitation or renovation should seek to preserve the character and history of the U.S. Capitol. New materials are expected to be of similar quality as existing, adjacent, historic, monumental examples: i. Dignity: Designs shall reflect the dignity that the citizens of the United States accord their Congress. ii. Long Life: Major facilities are designed for extremely long lives. Design shall provide for flexibility to allow for future change throughout the life of the building. iii.
